title: Void Ending in an Opposition to Venus
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The opposition is the hardest figure the Moon can close on: the text grades it as extreme enmity, because the signs it joins stand opposed across all four natural qualities. It shares with the square the warnings that guard every election, and a Moon waning in light and faced by Saturn is the source's own example of a serious misfortune.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with an opposition to Venus, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of her sweetness and her song. Venus governs taste, the text says, and with it beauty and love: poetic meter, songs, dancing, painting, and perfumes fall to her, with places of music and merriment among her locations. She is the Lesser Fortune, and her benevolence fits the works of youths, pleasures, and women. Pearls are her stones, the sweet smells are hers, and her colors are sky blue and gold fading into green.
